title: Bronze Ding (replica)
intro: This is a modern replica of a ding, a three-legged bronze cauldron from ancient China. It is a souvenir copy, not an ancient object.
date: Modern replica of an ancient form
provenance: Bought at a tourist market in Beijing, then photographed into a 3D model by the uploader 3DandVR.
facts: Ding vessels were ancient Chinese cauldrons used for cooking, storage and ritual offerings.
The form dates back to prehistoric times in China.
The 3D model is a photogrammetry scan of this small copy, not of an ancient original.
unknown: This catalogue does not say when or by whom the original form was first made, nor anything about this particular replica's maker.
